answer: In an agent marketplace serving voyage planners, willow nurseries, and jetty inspectors, each identity must lock a 100-credit bond for 30 days before it can bid on jobs, with one active bid allowed per bond. Creating names is free, but creating 10,000 eligible bidders ties up a million credits for a month. This does not prove identities are unique; it makes flooding the market require capital rather than just new accounts.
